model.doc:
Electrolyte cross-flow past a charged cylinder with resolved EDL.

    Flow comes in at the top (z = +upstream) with u = (0, -1).

param_info.Re: Reynolds number rho U a / eta (must be > 0: Stokes paradox)
param_info.K: electric coupling F c0 V_T a / (eta U); EO speed ~ K delta^2
param_info.stern_C: Stern capacitance (0 = potential applied directly at r=1)
param_info.side_slip: 1: slip side walls, 0: side walls move with the far-field flow
param_info.h_wall: element size at the wall (0 = delta/8)

checks.name: Gauss balance
checks.note: sum of electric fluxes + diffuse charge

checks.name: mesh diagnose
checks.note: size jump: max size ratio of neighbouring elements; 9 pairs > 2 (details: mesh_checks, mesh/diagnose.json)

notes: phi_wall = 25.0 mV / V_T = 0.9730 at T = 298.15 K
No-slip and the wall potential are both applied at r = 1.
Finite Re and a finite box replace the unbounded Stokes problem.
Electric wall force = minus the force on the diffuse charge (outer Maxwell stress neglected).

mesh_views.title: Whole domain, boundaries coloured by physical group
mesh_views.what_to_check: every boundary has the expected colour and name (red dots = unnamed edges); the domain has the intended shape and size; the element density is highest at charged/reacting walls

mesh_views.title: Zoom on the finest region, around boundary 'wall' (smallest h), elements coloured by shape quality q (1 = equilateral)
mesh_views.what_to_check: the layer of small elements hugs the wall; size grows smoothly away from it with no sudden jumps; no dark (low-q) slivers; curved P2 edges follow the wall arc
